messages.content: The museum has now confirmed that Wednesday's installation should finish at 5:00 p.m., so I no longer need the Thursday return. Please use Monday evening through Wednesday night, compare the flights and hotels, and put together the best itinerary for approval. Do not book anything yet.

Understood. I’ll revise the working dates to Monday, July 20 through Wednesday, July 22 and keep everything unbooked. For the outbound, the practical nonstop choices from Atlanta are Delta at 5:42 p.m., arriving St. Louis at 6:23 p.m., for $438 round trip when paired with the later Wednesday return, or Southwest at 7:05 p.m., arriving at 7:45 p.m., for $412 round trip. The Southwest fare includes two checked bags; the Delta fare is Main Cabin and excludes checked baggage.
The 5:42 departure is better. I do not want to arrive close to 8:00 when the review starts at 9:00 the next morning. What are the Wednesday returns with that outbound?

With Delta’s 5:42 p.m. Monday outbound, there are two nonstop Wednesday returns that follow the installation: 7:10 p.m. from St. Louis, arriving Atlanta at 9:42 p.m., for a $438 round-trip total, and 8:35 p.m., arriving at 11:07 p.m., for $461 round trip. The airport is about 20 to 30 minutes from the museum at that hour under ordinary traffic, but leaving the museum after 5:00 would make the 7:10 flight tight once the rental-car return and security time are included.
Agreed. Use the 8:35 return. Is there enough time if the work actually ends at 5:15?

Yes. Allowing 30 minutes to close out and leave the museum, roughly 30 minutes to reach the airport rental-car facility, 15 minutes for the return, and time for security still puts you at the terminal around 6:30 to 6:45 p.m. That leaves nearly two hours before the 8:35 departure. The flight pairing is Delta 5:42 p.m. Monday and 8:35 p.m. Wednesday at $461 in Main Cabin.
Check the seat maps before we go further. I need to know there is a reasonable seat on both legs, but still do not hold them.

The current seat maps show several standard Main Cabin seats available. On Monday, 14A, 14C, 15D, and 16F are open. On Wednesday, 12C, 13D, 15A, and 15F are open. Seat availability can change until ticketing, and nothing has been selected or held.
Use 14C going out and 12C coming back in the proposal. Now show me hotels for Monday and Tuesday nights, with the total after taxes and a realistic drive to the museum.

I found three workable two-night options. The Drury Plaza Hotel St. Louis at the Arch is $382.46 after taxes, with self-parking at $28 per night; the morning drive to the museum is usually 12 to 20 minutes. The Hampton Inn & Suites St. Louis at Forest Park is $417.08 after taxes, parking included, and generally 6 to 12 minutes from the museum. The AC Hotel St. Louis Central West End is $446.72 after taxes, valet parking at $40 per night, and about 5 to 10 minutes away. All three currently allow cancellation without charge until 6:00 p.m. local time on Sunday, July 19.
Does the Drury total include parking? Also, which museum address are you using for those times?

The Drury room total does not include parking. Adding two nights of self-parking brings its effective hotel cost to $438.46. I used the receiving museum’s project entrance on Fine Arts Drive, not the public visitor entrance, for all three drive estimates. Traffic around the downtown hotel creates the widest morning range.
Then compare Drury and Hampton more carefully. I care about the full cost and whether getting there by 8:30 Tuesday is dependable.

On full cost, Hampton is $21.38 less: $417.08 with parking included versus Drury at $438.46 including parking. For an 8:30 a.m. Tuesday arrival, I would plan to leave Hampton by 8:05; its route is short and avoids the downtown-to-park bottleneck. From Drury, a 7:50 departure would provide a similar cushion because congestion near downtown and the park approaches is less predictable. Both are viable, but Hampton has the simpler morning and lower effective total.
What kind of rooms are those prices for, and are they refundable rates rather than prepaid?

Drury is a refundable one-king room at $169 per night before taxes, payable at the hotel. Hampton is a refundable one-king room with a mini-fridge at $184 per night before taxes, also payable at the hotel. Neither quote is an advance-purchase rate. Hampton’s $417.08 total includes taxes and parking; incidental deposits are not included because they are released after checkout if unused.
Use Hampton. Check whether arriving after the Monday flight creates any check-in issue, and give me the rental-car figure too.

Hampton’s front desk operates around the clock. With the flight landing at 6:23 p.m., an estimated rental-car departure around 7:05, and a 20-to-25-minute drive, arrival should be around 7:30 p.m. There is no late-arrival issue, though the reservation can be noted for an evening arrival when booked. A midsize car from National for Monday 6:45 p.m. through Wednesday 6:30 p.m. is $176.34 including taxes and airport fees, with unlimited mileage. It is pay later; optional insurance, fuel, tolls, and parking away from the hotel are excluded.
That return time seems too early if I may not reach the airport until after 6:00.

You’re right. I checked a 7:00 p.m. return instead. The same midsize category remains $176.34 because the rental still falls within the same billing period. A 7:00 return gives the schedule room for a 5:15 finish, project closeout, and the drive to the airport without changing the quoted rate.
Good. Add up the flight, hotel, and car, and make sure the proposal clearly replaces the old three-night plan rather than leaving both versions active.

The revised working total is $1,054.42: Delta Main Cabin flights at $461.00, Hampton Inn & Suites St. Louis at Forest Park for two nights at $417.08, and the National midsize rental at $176.34. Airline checked-bag charges, fuel, meals, and incidental deposits are outside that figure. I have replaced the prior July 20–23 working plan with this July 20–22 version; there is only one active proposal, and no flight, hotel, car, or seat has been booked or held.
Please give me the approval-ready itinerary with the timing, room, cancellation deadline, seats, and the reason for taking the later return.

Approval proposal for the St. Louis installation: Monday, July 20, Delta nonstop departs Atlanta at 5:42 p.m. and arrives St. Louis at 6:23 p.m.; proposed Main Cabin seat 14C. Pick up a National midsize car at approximately 6:45 p.m. and check in that evening at Hampton Inn & Suites St. Louis at Forest Park. The refundable one-king room is reserved in the proposal for two nights, checking out Wednesday, July 22, at $417.08 including taxes and parking; cancellation is available without charge until 6:00 p.m. local time Sunday, July 19. Tuesday’s 9:00 a.m. condition review is supported by an 8:05 a.m. hotel departure for arrival around 8:15–8:25. Wednesday’s installation is scheduled to finish at 5:00 p.m.; the proposal allows for work through 5:15, closeout, and return of the car by 7:00 p.m. Delta then departs St. Louis nonstop at 8:35 p.m. and arrives Atlanta at 11:07 p.m.; proposed seat 12C. The later return avoids the compressed airport transfer required by the 7:10 flight. Total for flight, hotel, and car is $1,054.42, excluding checked-bag charges, fuel, meals, and incidentals. This replaces the earlier three-night itinerary. Nothing is booked or held, and seat availability must be rechecked when approval arrives.
